To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PAR-6 levels in Caenorhabdtis elegans are regulated by NOD-3 in a cullin dependent manner.
PAR-6 protein stability is regulated by the CBC/FEM-1 ubiquitin ligase in a cullin-dependent manner.
PAR-6 protein stability is regulated by the FEM-1/2 ubiquitin ligase and that this regulation is required for the establishment of polarity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate polarity in C. elegans.
the regulation of PAR proteins and polarity in Caenorhabitis elegans.
the identification and characterisation of upstream regulators of PAR proteins in C. elegans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PAR proteins are regulated in a cullin-dependent manner and that the FEM-1 protein plays a key role in the degradation of PAR-6.
PAR-6 protein is degraded in a CUL-dependent manner by the CBC(Fem) ubiquitin ligases.
NOS-3 regulates PAR-6 levels via a cullin-based ubiquitin ligases, which is required for PAR-6 stability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show that the PAR proteins have an evolutionarily conserved role in establishing polarity in C. elegans and mammals, and that the regulation of the PAR proteins by ubiquitin-dependent degradation is conserved in C. elegan s and mammals.
we have shown that NOS-3, FEM and CUL-2 regulate PAR-6 protein stability in C. elegans.
the FEM-1/2 adaptor protein regulates PAR-6 protein stability by targeting PAR-6 for proteasomal degradation in a CUL2 dependent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have uncovered a novel role for cullins and the FEM proteins in regulating PAR proteins.
we have identified a role for the CUL-2 ubiquitin ligase in the regulation of polarity proteins in Caenorhabditiis elegans.
we have identified a novel role for a cullin-dependent ubiquitin ligase in regulating the polarity protein PAR-6.
